title: Damped spring

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with exactly known physics (ω₀ = 11.18 rad/s, damping 0.35 /s)

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions or on-screen text indicate slow motion; motion appears as a continuous animation.

subjects.description: small green rectangular block attached to the bottom of a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A green block hanging from a vertical spring oscillates up and down above a black-and-white striped bar. The oscillation is already in progress at the start of the clip and continues without stopping through the end.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: s oscillates ~0 to 180 pixels with ~0.6 s period around ~90 pixels, peaks falling 180 to 150 and troughs rising 0 to 39, so underdamped harmonic motion in air. Candidates go from ideal to viscous exponential decay to nonlinear quadratic-drag and Coulomb decay to test which decay law extrapolates best.

law.title: Damped spring with linear air drag
law.summary: A spring block slows down a little each swing because air pushes against it.

params.name: gamma
params.meaning: viscous damping per mass, linear air drag

fitted.summary: A spring block slows down a little each swing because air pushes against it.

params.name: gamma

candidates.ifItWins: Amplitude decays exponentially, loss is viscous drag in air proportional to velocity.

law.title: Spring with linear plus quadratic air drag
law.summary: Air pushes much harder when the block moves fast than when it moves slow.

fitted.title: Spring with linear plus quadratic air drag
fitted.summary: Air pushes much harder when the block moves fast than when it moves slow.

candidates.ifItWins: Damping is faster at high speed than slow speed, air drag has a quadratic component.

law.title: Spring with air drag plus dry friction
law.summary: The spring loses a fixed bit of energy each swing from rubbing, plus a bit from air.

params.name: mu
params.meaning: Coulomb dry-friction deceleration, constant magnitude opposing motion

fitted.title: Spring with air drag plus dry friction
fitted.summary: The spring loses a fixed bit of energy each swing from rubbing, plus a bit from air.

params.name: mu
params.meaning: Coulomb dry-friction deceleration, constant magnitude opposing motion

candidates.ifItWins: Amplitude shrinks by the same amount each swing, there is dry rubbing in addition to air.

law.title: Ideal undamped spring-mass
law.summary: A block on a perfect spring bounces up and down forever with the same height.

fitted.title: Ideal undamped spring-mass

candidates.ifItWins: Amplitude does not decay, the spring is ideal and air losses are negligible over the clip.

caveats: Early frames show a few large outliers likely from stripe tracking
Mean miss shifts slightly from negative early to positive late
Quadratic drag and dry friction both fit to near zero and add nothing
critique.finding: The block swings around {s_eq} with natural tone {omega0} and slowly loses energy with damping {gamma}. It matches the motion closely with only a faint slow drift left in the misses.
critique.headline: Spring block slowly settles while it keeps swinging
critique.why_it_won: It includes gentle air damping that lets the swing shrink gradually, while the undamped spring keeps swinging too strongly and the projectile laws miss the back-and-forth entirely.

headline: Spring block slowly settles while it keeps swinging
finding: The block swings around 95.394 ± 0.067 pixel with natural tone 11.18100 ± 0.00094 1/s and slowly loses energy with damping 0.3504 ± 0.0017 1/s. It matches the motion closely with only a faint slow drift left in the misses.

eyeball.law_in_words: vertical mass on spring undergoes damped harmonic oscillation about equilibrium with linear viscous damping: acceleration equals -omega0 squared times displacement from s_eq minus gamma times velocity.
